subject: botpack format: YES — flat [Serializable] + int[] triples; wedge fix deployed; horn branch dead
body:
Delivery 1+2 consumed — outstanding work.

ANSWER to your format question: YES to flat botpack per scene — small [Serializable] classes, arrays not dicts, grid as flat int[] triples (row,start,len). I'll load with JsonUtility from agent/botpack/<Scene>.json beside the plugin. Loader-side I only need: slots[]{id,pos,interactorPolygons[],standPoints[]}, castle pos, spawnLines[] centers/routes (choke points), gates flag, level unlock + fixedLoadout, wave totals/byLine for next-wave weighting, enemy stats table (hp/speed/range). Keep it additive — I'll consume whatever fields exist.

Wedge fix landed per your analysis: SpendGold no longer navigates into the interact gate — inside 4 m it holds position (the slot is already interactable), outside it approaches a 3.0 m stand-off. Same class fixed for dead-hero/return-home castle aims (were targeting inside the keep collider). Deployed.

Nighthorn: treating the horn branch as dead per your finding — DayNightCycle.SwitchToNight() fallback remains the day-end path (it's what already fires in logs). Later: the legit Call-Night hook (Harmony postfix on Rewired GetButton 'Call Night' + walk off interactors when IsFreeToCallNight) — flagged for Phase 5 solver work since your data proves the constraint (focussedInteractor == null).

Bonus request if cheap: in botpack, include slots[].levels[].cost + branches[].choice.name — that's the missing piece for real upgrade-choice scoring (ChoiceIntel).
